newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian bonds firm ahead of big data week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian bonds firm ahead of big data week.

text.p: *Australian bonds built on their initial U.S.-led gains, but a further advance from here could prove a slow grind ahead next week's key data for inflation and wages.
*Imports data has little impact on market.
Australian bonds built on their initial U.S.-led gains, but a further advance from here could be restrained ahead next week's key data for inflation and wages.
And as U.S. Treasuries face very little data next week and over US$30 billion worth of supply in two and five year notes, they could give up some of Thursday's advance, traders said.
"We're back near the top of the range, so the upside is going to be a slow grind from here until the figures," one trader added.
However, local trading conditions were relatively light ahead of the weekend after two volatile sessions.

The 10-year bond continued Thursday's solid rebound after its yield touched 7.75 percent, but a break through 7.50 percent is expected to remain a stiff barrier until at least Wednesday's inflation and Thursday's wages report, traders said.
A string of bond friendly U.S. data, which suggested that the U.S. economy is slowing, helped support the local trend.
However, a flat outcome to the local September merchandise imports failed to inspire the market.
"Flat imports. A flat economy. No one will get carried away with these figures," said Han Kunnen, chief economist at Colonial State Bank.

Uncertainty over monetary policy after this week's RBA bulletin was further reflected in a flattening of the yield curve. The firm tone saw the Australian/U.S. 10-year bond yield spread narrow slightly, but N.Z. debt remained the week's star performer in the bloc, aided by a short-end stock squeeze.
